meta.pageTitle: GATE CSE Asymptotic Notation Previous Year Questions – Solved PYQs

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is TRUE for all positive functions [latex]f(n)[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Checking each option:
- Polynomial [latex]f(n)=n^k[/latex]: [latex]f(n^2)=n^{2k}[/latex] and [latex]f(n)^2=n^{2k}[/latex], so [latex]f(n^2)=\Theta(f(n)^2)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- [latex]f(n^2)=o(f(n)^2)[/latex] fails for polynomials (they are equal, not strictly smaller).
- For [latex]f(n)=2^n[/latex]: [latex]f(n^2)=2^{n^2}[/latex] but [latex]f(n)^2=2^{2n}[/latex]; [latex]2^{n^2}[/latex] grows much faster, so [latex]O[/latex] fails.
- For [latex]f(n)=2^{-n}[/latex]: [latex]f(n^2)=2^{-n^2}[/latex] is much smaller than [latex]f(n)^2=2^{-2n}[/latex], so [latex]\Omega[/latex] fails.

Answer: [latex]f(n^2)=\Theta(f(n)^2)[/latex], where f(n) is a polynomial

questions.text:
Consider the following three functions.

[latex]f_1=10^n\; f_2=n^{\log n}\;f_3=n^{\sqrt {n}}[/latex]

Which one of the following options arranges the functions in the increasing order of asymptotic growth rate?
questions.solution:
Write each as a power of 2:
- [latex]f_2=n^{\log n}=2^{(\log n)^2}[/latex]
- [latex]f_3=n^{\sqrt n}=2^{\sqrt n\log n}[/latex]
- [latex]f_1=10^n=2^{n\log10}[/latex]

Compare exponents: [latex](\log n)^2 \lt \sqrt n\log n \lt n\log 10[/latex] for large n.

Answer: [latex]f_2,f_3,f_1[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

The outer loop runs [latex]\log_2 n[/latex] times (i doubles) and the inner loop n times [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex].

[latex]O(n^2)[/latex], [latex]O(n\log n)[/latex] and [latex]O(n\log n\log n)[/latex] are valid upper bounds, but [latex]O(n)[/latex] is too small, so it is not a valid bound.

(This question was excluded from ISRO's evaluation because of its unclear wording.)

Answer: O(n)

questions.text: There are n unsorted arrays: [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex]. Assume that n is odd. Each of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] contains n distinct elements. There are no common elements between any two arrays. The worst-case Asymptotic Notation of computing the median of the medians of [latex]A_1,A_2,...,A_n[/latex] is ________ .
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Median of each unsorted array of n elements (linear-time selection): [latex]O(n)[/latex] each, n arrays [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(n^2)[/latex].
- Median of those n medians: [latex]O(n)[/latex].

Total [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]. It cannot be less, because all [latex]n^2[/latex] elements must be looked at.

Answer: [latex]O(n^2)[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

For each i, the inner loop runs about n/i times. Total [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac ni=n\cdot H_n=\Theta(n\log n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\theta(n\log n)[/latex]
